analysis.evidence: Mahalalel is the subject of וַיְחִי. The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת־יֶרֶד marks the birth of Jared as the starting point, and the following 830 years specify how long Mahalalel lived after that event.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.
analysis.sense: live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: מַהֲלַלְאֵל is the subject of וַיְחִי, “he lived.” The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת יֶרֶד, “after he fathered Jared,” identifies him as Jared’s father in the genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי introduces הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת יֶרֶד, “he fathered Jared.” The verse counts the 830 years Mahalalel lived after that event.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת יֶרֶד, “after he fathered Jared,” the suffix refers to Mahalalel, and אֶת marks Jared as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular subject suffix ־וֹ

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת יֶרֶד (“after he fathered Jared”), אֶת marks the proper name יֶרֶד as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for יֶרֶד linked to the root article yarad.
draft.definition: A masculine personal name borne here by Mahalalel’s son.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:16 counts the remaining years of Mahalalel’s life from the birth of Jared.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת יֶרֶד, “after he fathered Jared,” the suffix on הוֹלִידוֹ refers to Mahalalel, and אֶת marks יֶרֶד as the child he fathered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה means “thirty years.” The following וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה adds eight hundred years, giving 830 years that Mahalalel lived after fathering Jared.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural, absolute state

analysis.evidence: In שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה (“thirty years”), the marked noun supplies the unit counted by שְׁלֹשִׁים. The following eight hundred years bring the total to 830 years that Mahalalel lived after fathering Jared.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁמֹנֶה counts the hundreds. The conjunction adds these eight hundred years to the preceding שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה ‘thirty years’, giving 830 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral.
analysis.sense: eight as the multiplier of hundreds

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁמֹנֶה counts the hundreds, giving “and eight hundred years.”
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, used with both genders. No prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the singular noun supplies the unit for “eight hundred.” Together with the preceding thirty years, it gives the 830 years Mahalalel lived after fathering Jared.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מַהֲלַלְאֵל is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (“sons and daughters”) are its objects. After fathering Jared, Mahalalel fathered further children.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ
